citation: Wu et al. Discovering Invariant Rationales for Graph Neural Networks. ICLR 2022
notes: General method for interpretable GNNs, evaluated on graph classification. No security data.

citation: Wu et al. Handling Distribution Shifts on Graphs: An Invariance Perspective. ICLR 2022
notes: General method that helps GNNs make reliable predictions on graph-structured data even when the underlying data distribution changes.

citation: Gui et al. GOOD: A Graph Out-of-Distribution Benchmark. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 2022
notes: Benchmark containing graph datasets with different shift splits to evaluate OOD performance on GNNs

citation: Yehudai et al. From Local Structures to Size Generalization in Graph Neural Networks. Proceedings of the 38th International Conference on Machine Learning 2021
notes: A study proving why GNNs fail to generalize across graph sizes due to local structure discrepancies, alongside proposed solutions including a self-supervised task to improve size-generalization.

citation: Ying et al. Do Transformers Really Perform Badly for Graph Representation? Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 2021
notes: A Transformer-based model that incorporates spatial, centrality, and edge encodings to achieve competitive performance on graph representation learning tasks.

citation: Rampášek et al. Recipe for a General, Powerful, Scalable Graph Transformer. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 2022
notes: A modular Graph Transformer framework (GraphGPS) with linear time complexity that combines local message passing, global attention, and structural encodings for scalable graph learning.

citation: Shirzad et al. Exphormer: Sparse Transformers for Graphs. Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning 2023
notes: A sparse attention framework for graph transformers using expander graphs and virtual global nodes to achieve linear complexity and scalability to large graphs.

citation: Guo et al. Investigating Out-of-Distribution Generalization of GNNs: An Architecture Perspective. Proceedings of the 30th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining 2024
notes: An architectural study of GNN components under graph OOD settings, introducing a novel backbone model (DGat) that combines graph self-attention and decoupled architectures for improved generalization.

citation: Liao et al. Invariant Graph Transformer for Out-of-Distribution Generalization. Proceedings of the 32nd ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining V.1 2026
notes: An OOD-generalized Graph Transformer that disentangles invariant subgraphs via entropy-guided attention and dynamic subgraph encodings to handle distribution shifts.

citation: Cheng et al. KAIROS: Practical Intrusion Detection and Investigation using Whole-system Provenance. Symposium on Security and Privacy (S&P'24) 2024
notes: A PIDS using a GNN-based encoder-decoder to track structural changes over time and reconstruct compact summary graphs of attack activity.

citation: Rehman et al. Flash: A Comprehensive Approach to Intrusion Detection via Provenance Graph Representation Learning. IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (S&P), 2024.
notes: Uses a GNN on system-log graphs to find attacks. Passes all criteria. Provenance

citation: Xie and Liu. A Novel Hybrid Graph Neural Network and Transformer Model for Intrusion Detection. Peer-to-Peer Networking and Applications, 2026.
notes: Turns one traffic record into a tiny 8x8 image, then makes 16 patch nodes. The graph is not hosts or flows and never links different records. Network

citation: Appiahene et al. Network Intrusion Detection Using a Hybrid Graph-Based Convolutional Network and Transformer Architecture. PLOS ONE, 2026.
notes: Nodes are traffic records linked to similar records. Not a host-and-flow graph, so it fails our scope table. Network

citation: Zhang and Cao. A Hybrid Approach to Network Intrusion Detection Based on Graph Neural Networks and Transformer Architectures. 2024 14th ICIST, 2024.
notes: Hosts are nodes, flows are edges, GNN then Transformer. Passes all criteria. Network

citation: Bilot et al. Sometimes Simpler is Better: A Comprehensive Analysis of State-of-the-Art Provenance-Based Intrusion Detection Systems. USENIX Security Symposium, 2025.
notes: Evaluates 8 provenance IDSs (7 graph architectures) across OS audit logs. Provenance.

citation: Arp et al. Dos and Don'ts of Machine Learning in Computer Security. USENIX Security Symposium, 2022.
notes: Talks about mistakes in security ML in general. No graph detector. Background reading only

citation: Sarhan et al. NetFlow Datasets for Machine Learning-Based Network Intrusion Detection Systems. BDTA/WiCON, Springer, 2021.
notes: Builds NetFlow datasets and tests them with non-graph models. Background reading only

citation: Engelen et al. Troubleshooting an Intrusion Detection Dataset: the CICIDS2017 Case Study. IEEE Security and Privacy Workshops (SPW), 2021.
notes: Finds errors in the CICIDS2017 dataset. No detector proposed or tested. Background reading only

citation: Geirhos et al. Shortcut Learning in Deep Neural Networks. Nature Machine Intelligence, 2020.
notes: General paper on shortcut learning. No security data or detector. Background reading only

citation: Rosenfeld et al. The Risks of Invariant Risk Minimization. ICLR, 2021.
notes: Theory about invariant learning. No security data or detector. Background reading only

citation: Wiegreffe and Pinter. Attention is not not Explanation. EMNLP-IJCNLP 2019
notes: Challenges Jain and Wallace; proposes 4 tests of attention as explanation (uniform-weights baseline, seed-variance baseline, frozen-weight MLP diagnostic, adversarial training). BiLSTM with attention on SST, IMDB, AG News, 20 Newsgroups, MIMIC-III Diabetes and Anemia. No security data or detector. Background reading only

citation: Cohen et al. Certified Adversarial Robustness via Randomized Smoothing. ICML 2019
notes: Randomized smoothing: tight L2 certified-robustness bound for any base classifier under Gaussian noise. Image classifiers only (ResNet on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet). No security data or detector. Background reading only

citation: Taori et al. Measuring Robustness to Natural Distribution Shifts in Image Classification. NeurIPS 2020
notes: Meta-study of 204 ImageNet models in 213 test conditions; synthetic robustness does not transfer to natural shift (ImageNetV2, ObjectNet, video frames, ImageNet-A). Proposes the effective robustness metric. Image data only, no detector. Background reading only

citation: Sommer and Paxson. Outside the Closed World: On Using Machine Learning for Network Intrusion Detection. IEEE S&P 2010
notes: Position paper on why ML-based anomaly detection is rarely deployed for network intrusion detection (closed-world assumption, cost of errors, semantic gap, traffic diversity, evaluation problems) plus guidelines. No detector proposed or evaluated, no experiments, no graph input. Relevant to our evaluation criteria. Background reading only

citation: Gulrajani and Lopez-Paz. In Search of Lost Domain Generalization. ICLR 2021
notes: DomainBed testbed: 14 domain generalization algorithms, 7 image classification datasets (Colored MNIST, Rotated MNIST, PACS, VLCS, OfficeHome, TerraIncognita, DomainNet), 3 model selection rules; ResNet-50 and MNIST ConvNet. Finds tuned ERM matches all methods within 1 point and that model selection changes results. Image data only, no security data or detector. Background reading only

citation: Miller et al. Accuracy on the Line: On the Strong Correlation Between Out-of-Distribution and In-Distribution Generalization. ICML 2021
notes: Shows OOD accuracy is linearly correlated with ID accuracy (probit scale) across 3,000+ models on CIFAR-10 variants, ImageNet-V2, CINIC-10, STL-10, YCB-Objects pose, FMoW-WILDS and iWildCam-WILDS; weak on Camelyon17-WILDS and some CIFAR-10-C noise. Gaussian theory model. Image data only, no security data or detector. Background reading only

citation: Kazemnejad et al. The Impact of Positional Encoding on Length Generalization in Transformers. NeurIPS 2023
notes: Compares length generalization of decoder-only Transformers trained from scratch with APE, T5 relative PE, ALiBi, Rotary and no PE on 10 synthetic tasks (copy, reverse, addition, sorting, parity, LEGO, SCAN, PCFG, etc.); NoPE best. Appendix adds 1.3B code models on StarCoder. Sequence PEs, not graph PEs. No security data or detector. Background reading only

citation: Vaswani et al. Attention Is All You Need. NeurIPS 2017
notes: Original Transformer (multi-head self-attention, sinusoidal positional encoding) for machine translation on WMT 2014 En-De and En-Fr. No graph input, no security data or detector. Background reading only

citation: Jain and Wallace. Attention is not Explanation. NAACL-HLT 2019
notes: Shows attention weights correlate weakly with gradient and leave-one-out importance, and adversarial attention gives the same predictions. BiLSTM, CNN and average encoders on text classification (SST, IMDB, ADR Tweets, 20 Newsgroups, AG News, MIMIC-III), QA (CNN, bAbI) and NLI (SNLI). No security data or detector. Background reading only

citation: Sagawa et al. Distributionally Robust Neural Networks. ICLR 2020
notes: Group DRO for worst-group accuracy under spurious correlations; needs strong L2 penalty or early stopping to help overparameterized models; adds group adjustments and a stochastic optimizer. ResNet-50 on Waterbirds and CelebA, BERT on MultiNLI. No security data or detector. Background reading only
